message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"6","text":"For if you become occupied with the cares of ordinary life, you will lay an ambush for both yourself and your hearers. For because your occupations leave you unable to furnish what is beneficial as provisions, you will be punished for not teaching what is beneficial, while those who did not learn will perish, ignorance being the cause. Therefore, give them your undistracted time and preside over them, so that at the right time you may provide words capable of saving them. And so let them heed you, knowing that whatever the ambassador of the truth binds on earth has also been bound in heaven, and whatever he looses has been loosed. You, however, will bind what must be bound and loose what must be loosed. And as for the matters concerning you, the presiding officer, these are they, along with things like them.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"βιωτικαῖς μερίμναις ἀσχοληθῇς","chosen":"become occupied with the cares of ordinary life","rationale":"βιωτικός concerns ordinary worldly life, while ἀσχολέομαι emphasizes being occupied and deprived of leisure."},{"source_quote":"καὶ σεαυτὸν καὶ τοὺς ἀκροατὰς ἐνεδρεύσεις","chosen":"you will lay an ambush for both yourself and your hearers","rationale":"ἐνεδρεύω specifically evokes lying in ambush; the image is retained rather than generalized as merely endangering or ensnaring."},{"source_quote":"τὰ γὰρ συμφέροντα ἐφοδιάζειν","chosen":"to furnish what is beneficial as provisions","rationale":"ἐφοδιάζω evokes supplying provisions or equipping someone for a journey."},{"source_quote":"εὐσχολῶν προκαθέσθητι","chosen":"give them your undistracted time and preside over them","rationale":"εὐσχολέω contrasts with prior preoccupation, while προκαθέζομαι denotes taking the leading or presiding position."},{"source_quote":"ὁ τῆς ἀληθείας πρεσβευτὴς ὃ ἂν δήσῃ ἐπὶ γῆς, δέδεται καὶ ἐν οὐρανῷ","chosen":"whatever the ambassador of the truth binds on earth has also been bound in heaven","rationale":"πρεσβευτής denotes an authorized envoy, and the Greek perfect is retained rather than harmonized with a familiar future-tense rendering."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"οἱ δὲ μὴ μαθόντες ἀγνοίας αἰτία ἀπολοῦνται","issue":"The printed nominative αἰτία is syntactically abrupt. The translation understands it parenthetically as “ignorance being the cause”; a causal dative is a possible conjecture, but the supplied reading has not been replaced.","proposed_reading":"οἱ δὲ μὴ μαθόντες ἀγνοίας αἰτίᾳ ἀπολοῦνται","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"καὶ τὰ μὲν. κατὰ σὲ","issue":"The printed full stop interrupts the construction and separates μὲν from the phrase it appears to qualify. The translation reads the words as continuous in sense without treating the supplied punctuation as a transcription error.","proposed_reading":"καὶ τὰ μὲν κατὰ σὲ","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"7","text":"But let the duties concerning the elders be these: above all, let them quickly join the young in marriage, forestalling the snares of youthful desire. But let them not neglect marriage even for those already old, for in some people desire remains vigorous even after they have grown old. Therefore, so that sexual immorality may not gain ground against you and cast the same plague into your midst, take precautions beforehand and investigate whether the fire of adultery may be springing up secretly among you. For adultery is exceedingly terrible—so much so that it holds second place in punishment, since first place is awarded to those who are in error, even if they are chaste. Therefore, as elders of the church, train the Messiah’s bride in chastity (and by “bride” I mean the corporate body of the church). For if she is found chaste by the bridegroom king, she will obtain the greatest honor, and you, as those invited to the wedding, will enjoy great rejoicing. But if she is discovered to have sinned, she will be cast out, and you will pay the penalty—lest perhaps the sin have come about through your neglect.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"πρὸ πάντων τοὺς νέους πρὸς γάμον ζευγνύτωσαν ἐν τάχει","chosen":"above all, let them quickly join the young in marriage","rationale":"ζευγνύω literally joins or yokes together and here refers to arranging marriage."},{"source_quote":"τῆς νεαζούσης ἐπιθυμίας τὰ παγιδεύματα","chosen":"the snares of youthful desire","rationale":"The rendering preserves the trapping image of παγίδευμα and treats νεάζουσα as characterizing desire associated with youth."},{"source_quote":"ἡ πορνεία νομὴν λαβοῦσα καθ’ ὑμῶν","chosen":"sexual immorality may not gain ground against you","rationale":"νομὴν λαμβάνειν can describe spreading or gaining range, especially of disease or fire."},{"source_quote":"τοσοῦτον ὅσον τὰ δευτερεῖα ἔχειν αὐτὴν τῆς κολάσεως","chosen":"so much so that it holds second place in punishment","rationale":"δευτερεῖα denotes second rank or second prize; the ranking image is retained."},{"source_quote":"ἐπεὶ τὰ πρωτεῖα τοῖς ἐν πλάνῃ οὖσιν ἀποδίδοται, κἂν σωφρονῶσιν","chosen":"since first place is awarded to those who are in error, even if they are chaste","rationale":"πλάνη may denote doctrinal or moral error, but the text does not specify further; the surprising concession about chastity is preserved."},{"source_quote":"ἐξασκήσατε τὴν χριστοῦ νύμφην εἰς σωφροσύνην","chosen":"train the Messiah’s bride in chastity","rationale":"χριστοῦ stands independently as a designation and is therefore rendered titularly as “the Messiah’s,” while ἐξασκέω conveys disciplined training or cultivation."},{"source_quote":"νύμφην δὲ λέγω τῆς ἐκκλησίας τὸ σύστημα","chosen":"and by “bride” I mean the corporate body of the church","rationale":"σύστημα denotes an organized whole or collective body."},{"source_quote":"ὑμεῖς δὲ δίκην δώσετε μήπως παρὰ τὴν ὑμετέραν ἀμέλειαν γέγονεν ἡ ἁμαρτία","chosen":"and you will pay the penalty—lest perhaps the sin have come about through your neglect","rationale":"The rendering preserves the explicit future statement δίκην δώσετε and represents μήπως apprehensively rather than converting the entire statement into an unmarked conditional."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ὑμεῖς δὲ δίκην δώσετε μήπως παρὰ τὴν ὑμετέραν ἀμέλειαν γέγονεν ἡ ἁμαρτία","issue":"The dependency and force of μήπως are uncertain. It may have an apprehensive sense, “lest perhaps,” as translated, or introduce something closer to “whether perhaps”; taking it as “if perhaps” would make payment of the penalty conditional on negligence. The explicit assertion δίκην δώσετε remains independent in the translation.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"8","text":"Therefore, above all, concern yourselves with chastity, for sexual immorality has been decreed exceedingly grave in God’s sight. There are many kinds of sexual immorality, as Clement himself will also explain to you. But the first is adultery: a man’s not having relations only with his own wife, and a woman’s not having relations only with her own husband. If someone is chaste, he can also come to love humanity, for which reason he will obtain eternal mercy. Just as adultery is a great evil, so love for humanity is the greatest good. Therefore love all your brothers with reverent and merciful eyes, doing for orphans what parents do and for widows what husbands do, providing sustenance with complete gladness, marriages for those in their prime, and, for those among them without a trade, devising through occupations the means of necessary sustenance: work for a craftsperson, mercy for one who is inactive.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"λίαν γὰρ παρὰ τῷ θεῷ χαλεπὴ ὥρισται ἡ πορνεία","chosen":"sexual immorality has been decreed exceedingly grave in God’s sight","rationale":"ὁρίζω indicates authoritative determination, while χαλεπή here describes severity or gravity."},{"source_quote":"πορνείας δὲ εἴδη πολλά, ὡς καὶ αὐτὸς Κλήμης ὑμῖν διηγήσεται","chosen":"There are many kinds of sexual immorality, as Clement himself will also explain to you","rationale":"The translation preserves καί, which marks Clement himself as also supplying the promised explanation."},{"source_quote":"πλὴν πρώτη μοιχεία ἐστὶν","chosen":"But the first is adultery","rationale":"πρώτη is understood as the first of the previously mentioned kinds, without adding that it is necessarily the worst."},{"source_quote":"τὸ ἄνδρα μὴ ἰδίᾳ μόνῃ χρήσασθαι γυναικὶ καὶ γυναῖκα μὴ ἰδίῳ μόνῳ χρήσασθαι ἀνδρί","chosen":"a man’s not having relations only with his own wife, and a woman’s not having relations only with her own husband","rationale":"χρῆσθαι with a spouse in this context refers to sexual or marital relations; a literal rendering with “use” would mislead."},{"source_quote":"ἐὰν σώφρων ᾖ τις, καὶ φιλάνθρωπος γενέσθαι δύναται","chosen":"If someone is chaste, he can also come to love humanity","rationale":"The verbal English represents φιλάνθρωπος as an orientation of love toward humanity and keeps its human referent visible for consistency with the cognate noun."},{"source_quote":"ὡς δὲ ἡ μοιχεία μέγα κακόν, οὕτως ἡ φιλανθρωπία μέγιστον ἀγαθόν","chosen":"Just as adultery is a great evil, so love for humanity is the greatest good","rationale":"“Love for humanity” makes the components and human referent of φιλανθρωπία visible and supports the explicit contrast with μισανθρωπία in the following section."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς αὐτῶν ἀτέχνοις διὰ τῶν ἐπιτηδευμάτων ἐννοούμενοι τὰς προφάσεις τῆς ἀναγκαίας τροφῆς","chosen":"for those among them without a trade, devising through occupations the means of necessary sustenance","rationale":"ἀτέχνοις is taken as “unskilled” or “without a trade,” while προφάσεις denotes practical occasions or means in this context."},{"source_quote":"τεχνίτῃ ἔργον, ἀδρανεῖ ἔλεος","chosen":"work for a craftsperson, mercy for one who is inactive","rationale":"The compressed contrast assigns work to the craftsperson and charitable aid to the inactive person; ἀδρανής may imply idleness, inactivity, or inability to work."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"9","text":"I know that you will do these things if you establish love in your mind. There is one sufficient occasion for its entry: the common sharing of salt. Therefore make every effort to dine with one another more frequently, as you are able, so that you do not barter it away; for it is the cause of doing good, and doing good is the cause of salvation. All of you, then, make your means of life common to everyone who is a brother according to God, knowing that by giving temporary things you will receive eternal things. All the more, feed the hungry and provide drink to the thirsty, clothing to the naked; visit the sick; make yourselves present to those in prison and help them as you can; receive strangers into your own homes with complete eagerness. But, so that I do not speak item by item, love for humanity will teach you to do every good thing, just as hatred of humanity points out the practice of evil to those who do not wish to be saved.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"μία τις ἐστὶν ἱκανὴ πρόφασις, ἡ κοινὴ τῶν ἁλῶν μετάληψις","chosen":"There is one sufficient occasion for its entry: the common sharing of salt","rationale":"πρόφασις here denotes an occasion or means, while the specific salt image evokes shared food and table fellowship."},{"source_quote":"σπουδάζετε πυκνότερον συνέστιοι ἀλλήλων γίνεσθαι ὡς δύνασθε","chosen":"make every effort to dine with one another more frequently, as you are able","rationale":"σύνεστιος describes sharing a table or household meal; “more frequently” preserves the comparative πυκνότερον separately from the qualification of ability expressed by ὡς δύνασθε."},{"source_quote":"ὅπως αὐτὴν μὴ ἀπεμπολήσητε","chosen":"so that you do not barter it away","rationale":"The pronoun refers to love, and ἀπεμπολέω supplies a commercial image of selling or trading something away."},{"source_quote":"κοινοὺς οὖν πάντες πᾶσιν τοῖς κατὰ θεὸν ἀδελφοῖς τοὺς ἑαυτῶν παρέχετε βίους","chosen":"All of you, then, make your means of life common to everyone who is a brother according to God","rationale":"βίος can denote life, livelihood, or material means; the giving context favors “means of life” while retaining more breadth than “money.”"},{"source_quote":"τοῖς ἐν φυλακαῖς ἐπιφαινόμενοι ὡς δύνασθε βοηθεῖτε","chosen":"make yourselves present to those in prison and help them as you can","rationale":"ἐπιφαίνομαι literally denotes appearing or making oneself visible, here in the practical sense of visiting or being present."},{"source_quote":"ἵνα μὴ τὸ κατ᾽ εἶδος λέγω","chosen":"so that I do not speak item by item","rationale":"κατ᾽ εἶδος here means treating each matter separately by kind or category."},{"source_quote":"πᾶν καλὸν ἡ φιλανθρωπία ὑμᾶς ποιεῖν διδάξει, ὥσπερ ἡ μισανθρωπία τοῖς μὴ βουλομένοις σώζεσθαι τὴν κακοπραξίαν ὑποδείκνυσιν","chosen":"love for humanity will teach you to do every good thing, just as hatred of humanity points out the practice of evil to those who do not wish to be saved","rationale":"The matched phrases “love for humanity” and “hatred of humanity” preserve the explicit human referent and the lexical antithesis between φιλανθρωπία and μισανθρωπία."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"καὶ διψῶσι παρέχετε· ποτόν","issue":"The printed middle dot separates παρέχετε from ποτόν even though “drink” naturally serves as its object. The translation construes them together while disclosing the punctuation as supplied.","proposed_reading":"καὶ διψῶσι παρέχετε ποτόν","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"10","text":"Brothers who have disputes must not have their cases judged before the authorities, but must in every way be brought to agreement by the elders of the church, readily obeying them. Moreover, flee greed as something capable, under the pretext of temporary gain, of depriving you of eternal good things. Do you carefully observe balances, measures, and weights—the lawful standards of the localities? Act honorably with regard to deposits entrusted to you. Moreover, you will persevere in doing these and similar things to the end if you keep in your hearts an inseparable remembrance of the judgment that comes from God. For who could sin while fully convinced that judgment from the righteous God—who alone is now patient and good—has been appointed to take place at the completion of life, so that the good may thereafter enjoy the inexpressible good things everlastingly, while those found to be sinners, as evil people, will receive inexpressible punishment forever? And as for these things being so, if the prophet of the truth had not stated under oath that they would be, it might perhaps have been reasonable to doubt.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"οἱ πράγματα ἔχοντες ἀδελφοὶ","chosen":"Brothers who have disputes","rationale":"πράγματα ἔχειν in this legal setting refers to having cases, grievances, or disputes."},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ τῶν τῆς ἐκκλησίας πρεσβυτέρων συμβιβαζέσθωσαν παντὶ τρόπῳ","chosen":"must in every way be brought to agreement by the elders of the church","rationale":"συμβιβάζω here concerns reconciling the parties or settling their dispute."},{"source_quote":"πλὴν καὶ τὴν πλεονεξίαν οὕτως φεύγετε ὡς προφάσει προσκαίρου κέρδους ἀπὸ τῶν αἰωνίων ἀγαθῶν ζημιοῦν δυναμένην","chosen":"Moreover, flee greed as something capable, under the pretext of temporary gain, of depriving you of eternal good things","rationale":"The rendering preserves greed as the feminine referent of δυναμένην and retains the contrast between temporary gain and loss of eternal goods."},{"source_quote":"ζυγά, μέτρα, σταθμία, τὰ τῶντόπων δίκαια ἐπιμελῶς φυλάσσετε;","chosen":"Do you carefully observe balances, measures, and weights—the lawful standards of the localities?","rationale":"The supplied question punctuation is retained. The neuter phrase τὰ τῶντόπων δίκαια is construed appositionally as identifying the preceding balances, measures, and weights as the locally lawful standards."},{"source_quote":"πρὸς τὰς παρακαταθήκας εὐγνωμονεῖτε","chosen":"Act honorably with regard to deposits entrusted to you","rationale":"With entrusted property, εὐγνωμονέω denotes conscientious, fair, or honorable conduct rather than simple gratitude."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ νῦν μόνου μακροθύμου καὶ ἀγαθοῦ","chosen":"who alone is now patient and good","rationale":"μόνου is a genitive adjective agreeing with the reference to God, so “alone” qualifies God rather than imposing the temporal limitation “only for now.”"},{"source_quote":"τῶν ἀπορρήτων ἀγαθῶν ἀιδίως ἀπολαύσωσιν, οἱ δὲ ἁμαρτωλοὶ εὑρεθέντες ὡς κακοὶ ἀπορρήτου κολάσεως τεύξονται τὸν αἰῶνα","chosen":"enjoy the inexpressible good things everlastingly, while those found to be sinners, as evil people, will receive inexpressible punishment forever","rationale":"ἀπόρρητος is rendered consistently on both sides. The different temporal expressions remain visible as “everlastingly” for ἀιδίως and “forever” for the idiomatic τὸν αἰῶνα; the latter is literally “for the age” or “throughout the age,” but the change of expression does not by itself establish different durations."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τῶντόπων","issue":"The supplied print joins the article and noun without a space. This is an orthographic word-division feature and does not by itself create substantive uncertainty.","proposed_reading":"τῶν τόπων","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ζυγά, μέτρα, σταθμία, τὰ τῶντόπων δίκαια ἐπιμελῶς φυλάσσετε;","issue":"The supplied punctuation presents the sentence as a question, although φυλάσσετε can formally be read as either indicative or imperative. The translation retains the question. Syntactically, τὰ τῶντόπων δίκαια may appositionally identify the preceding balances, measures, and weights as the lawful local standards, as translated, or it may be a separate fourth object referring more generally to the lawful requirements of the localities.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἵνα οἱ ἀγαθοὶ τοῦ λοιποῦ τῶν ἀπορρήτων ἀγαθῶν ἀιδίως ἀπολαύσωσιν, οἱ δὲ ἁμαρτωλοὶ εὑρεθέντες ὡς κακοὶ ἀπορρήτου κολάσεως τεύξονται τὸν αἰῶνα","issue":"Within the result clause introduced by ἵνα, the first outcome uses the subjunctive ἀπολαύσωσιν, while the second shifts to the future indicative τεύξονται. The translation treats them as coordinated outcomes without correcting the grammatical shift.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
